name: volca sample2
about: A ten-part digital sample sequencer with 200 sample slots, a pitch and amp envelope per part and a shared reverb.
source: KORG volca sample (2nd generation) MIDI Implementation, Revision 1.00 (2022.11.01), https://www.korg.com/us/support/download/manual/0/867/4951/ ; MIDI Implementation Chart (Multi channel), Date Nov. 11 2020 v1.00, https://www.korg.com/us/support/download/manual/0/867/4821/ ; MIDI Implementation Chart (Single channel) https://www.korg.com/us/support/download/manual/0/867/4820/
notes: Factory default is multi-channel mode: Part 1-10 on MIDI channels 1-10, each triggered by note 48 and taking the same CCs on its own channel. Reverb Mix (CC 91) is received on channel 1 only. A single-channel mode (all parts on one global channel, selected by choosing a MIDI channel on the device) instead triggers the parts with notes 48-57 and uses different CC numbers per part (Part 1 Level 7, Pan 10; Part 2 Level 14, Pan 15, Speed 16, Amp Attack 17, Amp Decay 18, Hi Cut 19; and so on in blocks of six, with the rest by NRPN); this profile does not describe it. Sample number (CC 3 MSB 0-1 and CC 35 LSB 0-99, samples 0-199) is left out because it is not a 14-bit pair. Pan 0 and 1 both mean full left. Loop, Reverb and Reverse read 0-63 as Off and 64-127 as On. Clock, Start, Stop and Continue are received only when MIDI Clock Src is CL.At (the Auto setting); the txt lists Timing Clock, Start and Stop as transmitted. No Program Change is documented, so patterns cannot be selected by MIDI.
